title: Double-Entry Ledger
summary: A ledger is the system of record for money. Every movement is recorded as a balanced journal entry: debits equal credits, so money is never created or lost by a bug. Entries are append-only, so mistakes are fixed with new reversing entries, never edits. Balances are derived from the entries, and reconciliation checks the books against what the bank says actually happened.

walkthrough.title: Post a transaction
walkthrough.text: The payments service asks the ledger to record a $100 card payment: debit the customer's cash-in-transit account and credit the merchant's payable account. It includes an idempotency key.

walkthrough.title: Validate and write entries
walkthrough.text: The ledger checks that debits equal credits, that the accounts exist, and that the currencies match, then appends the lines to the immutable journal.

walkthrough.title: Update balances atomically
walkthrough.text: In the same database transaction, the account balances change with an optimistic version check, so two concurrent postings cannot both overdraw an account.

walkthrough.title: Return the entry
walkthrough.text: The caller gets an entry ID. Retrying with the same idempotency key returns the same entry rather than posting twice.

walkthrough.title: Reconcile with the bank
walkthrough.text: Each day the bank's settlement file is matched line by line against ledger entries for the clearing account. Every dollar must match.

walkthrough.title: Resolve breaks
walkthrough.text: Unmatched items, such as a missing settlement or a fee the bank deducted, become exceptions. They are fixed with new adjusting entries, never by editing history.

walkthrough.title: Close and report
walkthrough.text: At period end, balances are frozen, a trial balance checks that total debits equal total credits, and results export to the general ledger for finance.

data.label: Product Services
responsibilities: Describe business events as money movements between named accounts.
Send a stable idempotency key per business event so retries are safe.
Never keep their own balance; they ask the ledger.

failureModes.scenario: Timeout, then retry with a new key
failureModes.mitigation: Derive the key from the business event (e.g. paymentId:capture), not per attempt.

failureModes.impact: Two sources of truth drift apart.
failureModes.mitigation: The ledger is the only balance; services cache with clear staleness rules.

data.label: Ledger Service

input.name: Posting
input.type: lines: [{ account, debit|credit, amount: 10000, currency: USD }]

output.name: Transaction
output.type: One DB transaction: journal lines + balance updates

responsibilities: Rejects any posting where debits ≠ credits per currency.
Stores amounts as integers in minor units (cents); never floating point.
Enforces account rules such as 'customer wallet may not go negative'.

failureModes.mitigation: Integer minor units or fixed-precision decimals end to end.

failureModes.scenario: Hot account (one platform fee account) on every posting
failureModes.mitigation: Split the hot account into sub-accounts and sum them on read.

data.label: Journal (Append-Only)

input.name: Entry
input.type: entry_id, line_no, account_id, amount, direction, posted_at

responsibilities: Stores every journal line permanently: no UPDATE or DELETE is allowed.
Is the source of truth: any balance can be rebuilt by summing lines.
Provides an audit trail of who posted what, when, and why.

failureModes.impact: History no longer explains the balance; audit failure.
failureModes.mitigation: DB permissions without UPDATE/DELETE; corrections only as reversing entries.

failureModes.scenario: Table grows to billions of rows
failureModes.mitigation: Partition by month; archive closed periods to cheaper storage.

data.label: Account Balances

input.name: Delta
input.type: UPDATE … SET balance = balance - 10000, version = v+1 WHERE version = v

responsibilities: Keeps a running balance per account, updated in the same transaction as the journal.
Separates pending (authorised) from available (settled) funds.
Answers balance reads fast without summing history.

failureModes.scenario: Balance updated outside the journal transaction
failureModes.mitigation: Single ACID transaction; nightly job re-sums the journal and alerts on drift.
Version check or SELECT … FOR UPDATE; retry on conflict.

data.label: Reconciliation

input.name: Both sides
input.type: Ledger entries + bank / processor settlement lines

output.name: Result
output.type: Matched, plus exceptions: { missing, amount_mismatch, unknown }

responsibilities: Matches every external movement to a ledger entry by reference, amount, and date.
Raises exceptions for anything unmatched beyond a tolerance window.
Proves the ledger reflects reality, not just that it is internally consistent.

failureModes.scenario: Bank deducts fees inside a net settlement
failureModes.impact: Totals never match gross ledger entries.
failureModes.mitigation: Model fees explicitly and match the net amount as gross minus fees.
Ageing reports, ownership per exception type, and an SLA for resolution.

data.label: Banks & Processors

output.name: Statement
output.type: Daily file: credits, debits, fees, references

responsibilities: Report what money actually moved in real bank accounts.
Settle card and transfer batches, often a day or more later.
Provide the external truth the ledger is checked against.

failureModes.impact: Reconciliation cannot run; the close is delayed.
failureModes.mitigation: Schema validation, alerts on missing files, and API fallback.

failureModes.impact: Money counted as received is gone.
failureModes.mitigation: Track pending vs settled; post a reversal entry on return.

data.label: Close & Reporting

output.name: Reports
output.type: Trial balance, GL journal export, regulatory reports

responsibilities: Runs the trial balance: total debits must equal total credits.
Locks closed periods so late changes go into the current period.
Exports summarised entries to the company's general ledger.

failureModes.scenario: Posting backdated into a closed month
failureModes.impact: Published financials change after the fact.
failureModes.mitigation: Reject postings dated in closed periods; adjustments go into the current period.

failureModes.scenario: Trial balance does not net to zero
failureModes.impact: A bug created or destroyed money somewhere.
failureModes.mitigation: Run the check continuously, not just at close, and page someone on any non-zero result.
